subtasks.description: Declare all internal registers, wires, and parameters needed by the module: FSM state, next_state, transf_cnt, crc_c, buffer pointers, write_buf_0, write_buf_1, sd_data_out, last_din, data_send_index, crc_in, crc_en, crc_rst, crc_status, crc_s, busy_int, ack_transfer_int, ack_q, q_start_bit, output registers (DAT_oe_o, DAT_dat_o, rd, we, data_out, transm_complete, crc_ok, busy_n), and the flattened crc_out vector. Import parameters from sd_defines.v as specified in S005. Follow the interface ports defined in S001-S003 and internal signal widths in S004.
constraints: crc_out must be a scalar vector of width 16*SD_BUS_W, not an unpacked array or 2D vector.

subtasks.description: Instantiate one sd_crc_16 per data line (SD_BUS_W instances). Connect crc_in[i] to BITVAL, crc_en to Enable, crc_rst to RST, and assign each CRC output to the appropriate 16-bit slice of the flattened crc_out vector.
constraints: Use explicitly unrolled scalar instances; avoid generate/genvar constructs. Flatten crc_out as a single vector of width 16*SD_BUS_W with correct slice indexing.

subtasks.description: Implement a two‑stage flip‑flop synchronizer for ack_transfer: on posedge sd_clk, ack_q <= ack_transfer, then ack_transfer_int <= ack_q. Asynchronously clear both to 0 on rst.
Register q_start_bit: reset to 1; on sd_clk edge, if state == READ_WAIT and DAT_dat_i[0] == 0, set q_start_bit to 0; otherwise set it to 1.

Combinational logic that computes next_state from current state and inputs (start_dat, transf_cnt, crc_status, busy_int, DAT_dat_i[0]) as defined in the state transition table of S010. Covers all six states and default to IDLE.
Sequential block: on posedge sd_clk, state <= next_state; asynchronous reset sets state to IDLE.

Main output and control logic. On reset, assign all registers according to the S013 reset table. In normal operation, manage per‑state behavior: IDLE resets CRC/counters; WRITE_DAT loads buffers, serializes data with start/stop bits, delays DAT_dat_o via last_din, increments transf_cnt, and controls crc_en/crc_rst; WRITE_CRC captures CRC response token over 7 cycles into crc_s; WRITE_BUSY asserts transm_complete, sets crc_ok from crc_s, and polls DAT_dat_i[0] to deassert busy_n; READ_WAIT enables CRC and disables output; READ_DAT captures DAT_dat_i into data_out/we, increments transf_cnt, receives CRC bits, compares with crc_out, sets crc_ok and transm_complete, and clears busy_n.
constraints: All register arrays must be flattened into scalar signals; avoid unpacked arrays, generate blocks, or multidimensionals. Use plain always blocks.
